# Cocoa

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="cocoa-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="cocoa-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="cocoa-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Cadmium is the metal to check in cocoa: it rises with cocoa content, is highest in cocoa powder and dark chocolate, and is lowest in beans from West Africa; lead comes mainly from handling after harvest.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Eileen Abt, Jennifer Fong Sam, Patrick Gray, Lauren Posnick Robin · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market">Cadmium and Lead in Cocoa Powder and Chocolate Products in the U.S. Market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B Surveillance</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kataoka Y, Watanabe T, Hayashi K, Akiyama H · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium">Surveillance of Cadmium Concentration in Chocolate and Cocoa Powder Products Distributed in Japan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Hygiene and Safety Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. (ERG). Final Report dated March 28, 2022 (381 pp., including three technical attachments).</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals of concern:</strong>

Cadmium decides most cocoa questions; lead, nickel and aluminium are also elevated, while arsenic and mercury are usually low.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Eileen Abt, Jennifer Fong Sam, Patrick Gray, Lauren Posnick Robin · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market">Cadmium and Lead in Cocoa Powder and Chocolate Products in the U.S. Market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B Surveillance</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2015-nickel-food-water|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2015-nickel-food-water">Scientific Opinion on the risks to public health related to the presence of nickel in food and drinking water</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2015;13(2):4002, 202 pp.</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2015-nickel-food-water">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Growing origin, soil cadmium and pH, and cocoa content for cadmium; shell, dust and handling for lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kataoka Y, Watanabe T, Hayashi K, Akiyama H · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium">Surveillance of Cadmium Concentration in Chocolate and Cocoa Powder Products Distributed in Japan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Hygiene and Safety Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. (ERG). Final Report dated March 28, 2022 (381 pp., including three technical attachments).</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/wade2022-cacao-cadmium-drivers|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wade J, Ac-Pangan M, Favoretto VR, Taylor AJ, Engeseth N, Margenot AJ · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wade2022-cacao-cadmium-drivers">Drivers of cadmium accumulation in Theobroma cacao L. beans: A quantitative synthesis of soil-plant relationships across the Cacao Belt</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLOS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wade2022-cacao-cadmium-drivers">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot cadmium results with the cocoa-solids content, and cleaning and shelling controls for lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. (ERG). Final Report dated March 28, 2022 (381 pp., including three technical attachments).</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
</ul>
</section>

<a id="cocoa-overview"></a>
<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Cocoa overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Cadmium is the metal that sets cocoa apart, and it travels with the cocoa solids. In the US retail survey by Abt and colleagues, mean cadmium was 700 µg/kg in cocoa powder, 270 µg/kg in dark chocolate and 60 µg/kg in milk chocolate.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Eileen Abt, Jennifer Fong Sam, Patrick Gray, Lauren Posnick Robin · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market">Cadmium and Lead in Cocoa Powder and Chocolate Products in the U.S. Market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B Surveillance</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Japan, the median rose from 23 µg/kg in chocolate under 50% cocoa to 250 µg/kg at 80% or more.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kataoka Y, Watanabe T, Hayashi K, Akiyama H · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium">Surveillance of Cadmium Concentration in Chocolate and Cocoa Powder Products Distributed in Japan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Hygiene and Safety Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Lead, by contrast, is usually lower and is driven more by what happens to the bean after harvest than by where it grew.<sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. (ERG). Final Report dated March 28, 2022 (381 pp., including three technical attachments).</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/abt2020-perspective-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Eileen Abt, Lauren Posnick Robin · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abt2020-perspective-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate">Perspective on Cadmium and Lead in Cocoa and Chocolate</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abt2020-perspective-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Growing origin is the strongest supported lever for cadmium. In industry bean testing compiled for a California settlement, median bean cadmium was 55 to 94 µg/kg for Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Cameroon and Brazil, against 511 µg/kg for Ecuador, 542 µg/kg for Peru and 892 µg/kg for Venezuela.<sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. (ERG). Final Report dated March 28, 2022 (381 pp., including three technical attachments).</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The international cadmium assessment found the same pattern in cocoa powder, with a mean of 141 µg/kg in the mainly African cluster and 1,601 µg/kg in the mainly South and Central American cluster.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: dietary exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Food Additives Series, No. 82 (Safety evaluation of certain contaminants in food, prepared by the 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The low-cadmium origins are not lower in lead, so origin choice addresses one metal, not both.<sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. (ERG). Final Report dated March 28, 2022 (381 pp., including three technical attachments).</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ferreira de Oliveira AP, Milani RF, Efraim P, Morgano MA, Tfouni SAV · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Cd and Pb in cocoa beans: Occurrence and effects of chocolate processing</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Control 119, 107455</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer, the supported priorities are lot results for cadmium with the cocoa-solids content stated, and cleaning and shelling controls for lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. <a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as cocoa

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

Cocoa comes from the seeds of Theobroma cacao, which are fermented, dried, cleaned and roasted, then separated into shell and nib.<sup class="cite">[[sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ferreira de Oliveira AP, Milani RF, Efraim P, Morgano MA, Tfouni SAV · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Cd and Pb in cocoa beans: Occurrence and effects of chocolate processing</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Control 119, 107455</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxc-81-2022|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxc-81-2022">Code of Practice for the Prevention and Reduction of Cadmium Contamination in Cocoa Beans (CXC 81-2022)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FAO and WHO, 2023. Codex Alimentarius Code of Practice No. CXC 81-2022. Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme. Rome.</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxc-81-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Ground nibs form cocoa liquor, which is pressed into cocoa butter and a cake milled into cocoa powder; chocolate combines liquor, butter, sugar and, in milk chocolate, milk solids.<sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-cocoa" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-cocoa-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one subgroup, cocoa form and metal. Percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Ratings place a reported mean, median or single result against a pooled HMI reference for the same form (beans and nibs, liquor, butter, powder, sweetened powder, and each chocolate type), built from every compatible sampling family. Same-study contrasts compare a subgroup with its own study total for that form. Held rows failed a check against their own paper and are shown but not compared.</p>

Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>180</td><td>819</td><td>2170</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>206</td><td>819</td><td>2170</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>87 reference units; 7 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>22</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Eileen et al. 2018</td><td>7</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Barraza et al. 2019</td><td>4</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Blommaert et al. 2022</td><td>2</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Ferreira et al. 2021</td><td>9</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Burgon 2023</td><td>1</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>As You Sow 2022</td><td>42</td><td>14%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for cocoa beans and nibs from every compatible sampling family in the cocoa evidence ledger: WHO GEMS/Food region-by-year medians (random sampling, individual records only), FDA Total Diet Study composites where they exist, individual products or batches printed by surveys, and published subgroup medians. Each family has equal total weight; subgroups have equal weight within a family. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges, maxima and values quoted from other studies never enter as observations.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1, Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>An international evidence-library reference for cocoa beans and nibs, not a probability sample of any market. GEMS/Food regions are reporting regions, not growing origins. Many submissions are non-detects with differing limits, which widens the bounds. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Collection period</p><p data-timeline-scope>2014 to 2020</p><div data-selected-timeline><p>No year-by-year sample register is reconstructed from this summary.</p></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Geographic scope</p><p data-regional-scope>Unknown</p><div data-selected-regional><p>Reported growing origin.</p></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Sampling, analysis and reporting limits</p><p>SD: &#39;ICP Mass Spec&#39; (12 samples GFAAS), no further details; AYS: commercial labs, method by product record; Ecuador and factory: ICP-MS (EPA 6020A, ALS; Eurofins).</p><p>SD data gave no LOD/LOQ; values flagged &#39;&lt;&#39; were treated by the Expert Committee as non-detects and replaced with presumed LOD/sqrt(2) for descriptive statistics; reported zeros counted as non-detects for DF but excluded from statistics. DF = detection frequency.</p><p>The value conflicts with its own paper: &gt;=500 ppb 0.01% is not attainable with n=1024 (no whole number of samples gives this percentage) Reported material: chocolate (cocoa) liquor (Batch 1). Settling Defendant (industry) testing data, blinded and compiled; no methods, LOD, QA/QC or sampling protocol supplied (Root Cause Report s.3.2). Expert Committee could not disclose ranges/min/max (confidentiality). Some samples may have been collected in Whirl-Pak bags (possible contamination concern for liquor). Exceedance profile (percent of samples at or above 3/10/50/100/250/500 ppb). Statistic &#39;percentile&#39; used because schema has no exceedance statistic; values are in exceedance_profile_percent.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Shared samples and study overlap</p><p>Subgroup rows, statistics of the same subgroup and the study total share samples; they are not independent results.</p><p>Each table row describes a food/analyte result. class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wade J, Ac-Pangan M, Favoretto VR, Taylor AJ, Engeseth N, Margenot AJ · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" nib cadmium tracked leaf cadmium closely (r = 0.79) but total soil cadmium only weakly (r = 0.35).<sup class="cite">[[sources/ramtahal2016-cacao-cadmium-trinidad|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span Within the tree, cadmium reaching the nib travels mainly through the branches rather than from the leaves.<sup class="cite">[[sources/blommaert2022-cd-cacao-translocation|22]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Blommaert H, Aucour A-M, Wiggenhauser M, Moens C, Telouk P, Campillo S, Beauchêne J, Landrot G, Testemale D, Pin S, Lewis <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-chocolate-types-have-the-least-cadmium" data-anchor="which-chocolate-types-have-the-least-cadmium" data-question="Which chocolate types have the least cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which chocolate types have the least cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Milk chocolate and white chocolate, because cadmium follows the nonfat cocoa solids.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Eileen Abt, Jennifer Fong Sam, Patrick Gray, Lauren Posnick Robin · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market">Cadmium and Lead in Cocoa Powder and Chocolate Products in the U.S. Market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; <a id="processing-effects-and-derivatives"></a>
## Processing, fermentation and shelling

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Processing redistributes metals between fractions rather than removing them.<sup class="cite">[[sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ferreira de Oliveira AP, Milani RF, Efraim P, Morgano MA, Tfouni SAV · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Cd and Pb in cocoa beans: Occurrence and effects of chocolate processing</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Control 119, 107455</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In the Bahia pilot run, about 59% of the cadmium stayed in the mill residue, 35% went to the liquor and 6% to the shell, and pressing sent all of the liquor’s cadmium into the cake and none into the butter.<sup class="cite">[[sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ferreira de Oliveira AP, Milani RF, Efraim P, Morgano MA, Tfouni SAV · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Cd and Pb in cocoa beans: Occurrence and effects of chocolate processing</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Control 119, 107455</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> That is why cocoa powder, the defatted solids, is the most concentrated retail form, while cocoa butter is low.<sup class="cite">[[sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ferreira de Oliveira AP, Milani RF, Efraim P, Morgano MA, Tfouni SAV · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Cd and Pb in cocoa beans: Occurrence and effects of chocolate processing</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Control 119, 107455</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For lead, cleaning and shelling are the steps with measured effects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. Final Report dated March 28, 2022 (381 pp., including three technical attachments).</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Fermentation has only small tested effects on cadmium. Adding Rhizobium japonicum to the fermenting mass lowered Trinitario bean cadmium from 0.36 to 0.29 to 0.30 mg/kg but barely changed Nacional beans (0.34 to 0.35 mg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/chang2022-cocoa-fermentation-rhizobium-cadmium|28]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Chang JV, Cortez LV, Solorzano CE, Flor FI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chang2022-cocoa-fermentation-rhizobium-cadmium">Induction of rhizobium japonicum in the fermentative mass of two varieties of cacao (Theobroma Cacao L.) as a strategy for the decrease of cadmium</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Health Sciences</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chang2022-cocoa-fermentation-rhizobium-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A review notes that cadmium can move from nib to shell when fermentation drives nib pH below 5, which is a mechanism rather than a validated control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abt2020-perspective-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Eileen Abt, Lauren Posnick Robin · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abt2020-perspective-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate">Perspective on Cadmium and Lead in Cocoa and Chocolate</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abt2020-perspective-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-cocoa-butter-contain-heavy-metals" data-anchor="does-cocoa-butter-contain-heavy-metals" data-question="Does cocoa butter contain heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does cocoa butter contain heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Very little cadmium: in the Brazilian pilot run, butter was below 1.5 µg/kg while the powder from the same batch held 111 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ferreira de Oliveira AP, Milani RF, Efraim P, Morgano MA, Tfouni SAV · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Cd and Pb in cocoa beans: Occurrence and effects of chocolate processing</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Control 119, 107455</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oliveira2021-cocoa-beans-cd-pb-brazil-processing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> International data put the global median for cocoa butter at 20 µg/kg cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: dietary exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Food Additives Series, No. 82 (Safety evaluation of certain contaminants in food, prepared by the 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>


<a id="heavy-metal-mitigation-and-remediation-for-cocoa"></a>
<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation from farm to factory

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

Controls for cocoa act at the farm, during post-harvest handling, in the factory and at lot acceptance.<sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxc-81-2022|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxc-81-2022">Code of Practice for the Prevention and Reduction of Cadmium Contamination in Cocoa Beans (CXC 81-2022)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FAO and WHO, 2023. Codex Alimentarius Code of Practice No. CXC 81-2022. Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme. Rome.</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxc-81-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The Codex code of practice recommends soil testing, liming toward pH 6 or above (for example 3 t/ha/year of dolomite), avoiding cadmium-rich fertilisers, applying zinc and using low-cadmium planting material, but it reports no measured effect sizes.<sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxc-81-2022|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxc-81-2022">Code of Practice for the Prevention and Reduction of Cadmium Contamination in Cocoa Beans (CXC 81-2022)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FAO and WHO, 2023. Codex Alimentarius Code of Practice No. CXC 81-2022. Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme. Rome.</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxc-81-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

The field evidence for cadmium is limited but measurable. In a Peruvian field trial, arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi lowered bean cadmium from 0.94 to 0.56 mg/kg, while biochar at 1 to 2% had smaller effects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/vega-jara2025-cocoa-cd-mitigation-amf-biochar|29]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Vega-Jara L, Palacin Agüero J, Farfán Tucto S, Vangeli S, Márquez-Dávila K · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/vega-jara2025-cocoa-cd-mitigation-amf-biochar">Mitigation of Cadmium Accumulation in Cocoa Beans Using Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi, Biochar and Callisia repens</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Folia Amazónica</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/vega-jara2025-cocoa-cd-mitigation-amf-biochar">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In a greenhouse trial, quinoa biochar at 2% cut seedling leaf cadmium by 15 to 54% depending on soil, but beans were not measured.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopez2022-cacao-biochar-cadmium|30]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Julian E. Lopez, Catalina Arroyave, Adriana Aristizabal, Byrone Almeida, Santiago Builes, Eduardo Chavez · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopez2022-cacao-biochar-cadmium">Reducing cadmium bioaccumulation in Theobroma cacao using biochar: basis for scaling-up to field</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Heliyon</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopez2022-cacao-biochar-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Compost changed soil cadmium fractions in Ecuador, but the bean results were not printed.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gutierrez2022-ecuador-cacao-cadmium-compost|31]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gutiérrez E, Chávez E, Gamage KHH, Argüello D, Galkaduwa MB, Hettiarachchi GM · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gutierrez2022-ecuador-cacao-cadmium-compost">Cadmium fractionation in soils affected by organic matter application: Transfer of cadmium to cacao (Theobroma cacao L.) tissues</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Environmental Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gutierrez2022-ecuador-cacao-cadmium-compost">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Lead controls are about cleanliness after harvest: drying beans off the ground, cleaning, removing shells and dust, and keeping equipment free of lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. (ERG). Final Report dated March 28, 2022 (381 pp., including three technical attachments).</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxc-81-2022|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxc-81-2022">Code of Practice for the Prevention and Reduction of Cadmium Contamination in Cocoa Beans (CXC 81-2022)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FAO and WHO, 2023. Codex Alimentarius Code of Practice No. CXC 81-2022. Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme. Rome.</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxc-81-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Testing detects contamination and supports exclusion or blending, but it does not remove metals.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: dietary exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Food Additives Series, No. 82 (Safety evaluation of certain contaminants in food, prepared by the 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/meter2019-cadmium-cacao-lac-review|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Meter A, Atkinson RJ, Laliberte B · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/meter2019-cadmium-cacao-lac-review">Cadmium in Cacao from Latin America and the Caribbean: A Review of Research and Potential Mitigation Solutions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bioversity International / CAF Development Bank of Latin America</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/meter2019-cadmium-cacao-lac-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>

<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Switching origin to reduce cadmium can leave lead unchanged or higher. West African beans had the lowest cadmium medians but lead medians of about 25 µg/kg, while Ecuadorian and Peruvian beans were higher in cadmium and lower in lead in the same industry testing.<sup class="cite">[[sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahn, Timothy, Chaney, Rufus L., DiBartolomeis, Michael J., Ramtahal, Gideon · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Expert Investigation Related to Cocoa and Chocolate Products: Final Report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Expert Committee report submitted to As You Sow and the Settling Defendants under a California Proposition 65 Consent Judgment; Project Manager: Eastern Research Group, Inc. (ERG). Final Report dated March 28, 2022 (381 pp., including three technical attachments).</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/asyousow2022-expert-investigation-cocoa-chocolate-products">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Soil amendments are not uniformly effective. A review found that gypsum, or lime with compost, lowered leaf cadmium but not bean cadmium in some trials, and that some liming materials increased uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/garciaporras2025-cadmium-cacao-farmland|33]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">García Porras GA, Santos JAd, Carvalho MRd, Pinzón-Sandoval EH, Pereira AAS, Guilherme LRG · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/garciaporras2025-cadmium-cacao-farmland">Addressing Cadmium in Cacao Farmland: A Path to Safer, Sustainable Chocolate</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Agriculture</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/garciaporras2025-cadmium-cacao-farmland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Biochar effects were not statistically significant in every soil tested.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopez2022-cacao-biochar-cadmium|30]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Julian E. Lopez, Catalina Arroyave, Adriana Aristizabal, Byrone Almeida, Santiago Builes, Eduardo Chavez · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopez2022-cacao-biochar-cadmium">Reducing cadmium bioaccumulation in Theobroma cacao using biochar: basis for scaling-up to field</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Heliyon</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopez2022-cacao-biochar-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Blending dilutes a high-cadmium lot rather than removing cadmium, and a lower-cocoa recipe lowers cadmium per gram of chocolate but not per gram of cocoa.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kataoka Y, Watanabe T, Hayashi K, Akiyama H · class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Meter A, Atkinson RJ, Laliberte B · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/meter2019-cadmium-cacao-lac-review">Cadmium in Cacao control: certified-organic products measured higher in the US analysis.<sup class="cite">[[sources/hands2024-multiyear-dark-chocolate-cocoa-usa|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span ## Testing cocoa for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-027"></a>
<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

A useful cocoa test states the form, the basis and the cocoa-solids content, because the EU and Codex limits are set by cocoa-solids class.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Beans are usually reported on a dry-weight basis and products as sold; Singapore’s cocoa-powder limits are even set on a dry, fat-free basis.<sup class="cite">[[sources/arevalo-gardini2017-peru-cacao-regional-metals|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Arévalo-Gardini E, Arévalo-Hernández CO, Baligar VC, He ZL · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/arevalo-gardini2017-peru-cacao-regional-metals">Heavy metal accumulation in leaves and beans of cacao (Theobroma cacao L.) in major cacao growing regions in Peru</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Science of the Total Environment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/arevalo-gardini2017-peru-cacao-regional-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/sfa2026-food-regulations-heavy-metals|34]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Singapore Food Agency · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sfa2026-food-regulations-heavy-metals">Food Regulations: regulation 31 heavy metals, arsenic and lead</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Singapore Statutes Online</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sfa2026-food-regulations-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Detection limits must sit well below the relevant limit. FDA’s reporting limits were 3 µg/kg for cadmium and 10 µg/kg for lead in cocoa powder, while some monitoring submissions used limits of 40 µg/kg or more for cadmium in powder, which hides much of the lower range.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Several surveys reported no detection limit, reference material or recovery check, and two were held here because their values could not be reconciled with their own methods.<sup class="cite">[[sources/amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Amjad M, Hussain S, Baloch ZU, Raza A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Locally Available Chocolates in Lahore Region</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/enogbe2025-bwari-chocolate-metals|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Emmanuel Joy Enogbe, Agbaghare Daniel Enajeme · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/enogbe2025-bwari-chocolate-metals">Levels of heavy metals concentrations in chocolates from Bwari market Abuja FCT, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Adulteration9:e2ijad3057</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/enogbe2025-bwari-chocolate-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Arsenic and mercury in cocoa are reported almost entirely as totals.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-arsenic-contam-2009|35]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa-arsenic-contam-2009">Scientific Opinion on Arsenic in Food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2009;7(10):1351</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-arsenic-contam-2009">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Inorganic arsenic in European monitoring of chocolate and cocoa powder was mostly below about 20 µg/kg, and no source measured methylmercury or hexavalent chromium in cocoa.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="why-do-some-surveys-report-very-high-metals-in-chocolate" data-anchor="why-do-some-surveys-report-very-high-metals-in-chocolate" data-question="Why do some surveys report very high metals in chocolate?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Why do some surveys report very high metals in chocolate?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Some very high values come from products that are mostly not cocoa or from methods that cannot support them. A Lahore survey converted digest results with inconsistent factors and included many compound confections without cocoa, and an Abuja survey reported chromium 30 to 40 times the limit it cited while concluding compliance.<sup class="cite">[[sources/amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Amjad M, Hussain S, Baloch ZU, Raza A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Locally Available Chocolates in Lahore Region</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/enogbe2025-bwari-chocolate-metals|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Emmanuel Joy Enogbe, Agbaghare Daniel Enajeme · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/enogbe2025-bwari-chocolate-metals">Levels of heavy metals concentrations in chocolates from Bwari market Abuja FCT, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Adulteration9:e2ijad3057</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/enogbe2025-bwari-chocolate-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> EFSA found that chocolate products supplied 4.3% of cadmium exposure across European age groups, and close to 10% for school-age children when cocoa beans and products are added.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Cadmium dietary exposure in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2012;10(1):2551</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> JECFA put cocoa products at 0.1 to 9.4% of cadmium exposure across national and regional diets and concluded they are not a major contributor; applying the Codex limits lowered total exposure by 0.7% on average.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: dietary exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Food Additives Series, No. 82 (Safety evaluation of certain contaminants in food, prepared by the 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Chocolate matters more for nickel. EFSA found that sugar and confectionery, driven mainly by chocolate, supplied up to 31% of adolescents’ nickel exposure, and cocoa beverages, with soft drinks, were the main beverage contributors for toddlers.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-nickel-contam-2020|40]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa-nickel-contam-2020">Update of the Risk Assessment of Nickel in Food and Drinking Water</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2020;18(11):6268</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-nickel-contam-2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Concentration is not intake: a small serving of dark chocolate can add more cadmium than a larger serving of milk chocolate.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Eileen Abt, Jennifer Fong Sam, Patrick Gray, Lauren Posnick Robin · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market">Cadmium and Lead in Cocoa Powder and Chocolate Products in the U.S. Market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B Surveillance</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abt2018-cadmium-lead-cocoa-chocolate-us-market">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kataoka Y, Watanabe T, Hayashi K, Akiyama H · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium">Surveillance of Cadmium Concentration in Chocolate and Cocoa Powder Products Distributed in Japan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Hygiene and Safety Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kataoka2018-japan-chocolate-cocoa-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Australian milk chocolate averaged 15 µg/kg cadmium and 6 µg/kg lead in the 25th total diet study, near the low end of retail chocolate.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study|41]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">25th Australian Total Diet Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

## Evidence review and remaining gaps

<a id="hmi-ing-034"></a>
<a id="which-primary-regulatory-instruments-apply-to-this-exact-ingredient-form-species-market-and-date"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-035"></a>
<a id="what-searches-eligibility-decisions-source-families-and-appraisal-underpin-the-answers-and-certainty-judgments"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-036"></a>
<a id="what-remains-unresolved-when-was-each-answer-reviewed-and-what-changed-in-this-version"></a>

This assessment covers every source record in the HMI library that is tagged to cocoa or mentions cocoa, cacao or chocolate, plus every matching row in WHO GEMS/Food, the FDA Total Diet Study and other indexed datasets, each with a recorded decision based on its content. Two retail surveys are held in full and individual values from several others are held because they could not be reconciled with their own methods or figures.<sup class="cite">[[sources/amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Amjad M, Hussain S, Baloch ZU, Raza A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals">Determination of Heavy Metals in Locally Available Chocolates in Lahore Region</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/enogbe2025-bwari-chocolate-metals|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Emmanuel Joy Enogbe, Agbaghare Daniel Enajeme · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/enogbe2025-bwari-chocolate-metals">Levels of heavy metals concentrations in chocolates from Bwari market Abuja FCT, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Adulteration9:e2ijad3057</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/enogbe2025-bwari-chocolate-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/romero-estevez2019-ecuador-cocoa-cd-ni-pb|20]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Romero-Estevez D, Yanez-Jacome GS, Simbana-Farinango K, Navarrete H · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/romero-estevez2019-ecuador-cocoa-cd-ni-pb">Content and the relationship between cadmium, nickel, and lead concentrations in Ecuadorian cocoa beans from nine provinces</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Control</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/romero-estevez2019-ecuador-cocoa-cd-ni-pb">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

The remaining gaps are mostly unpublished data. Per-farm bean results behind the Ecuadorian compost trial and the Peruvian national map, per-product values behind the multi-year US analysis, and EFSA’s 2020 nickel annex were not available in the library.<sup class="cite">[[sources/thomas2023-peru-cacao-cd-distribution|23]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Thomas E, Atkinson R, Zavaleta D, Rodriguez C, Lastra S, Yovera F, Arango K, Pezo A, Aguilar J, Tames M, Ramos A, Cruz W, Cosme R, Espinoza E, Chavez CR, Ladd B · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/thomas2023-peru-cacao-cd-distribution">The distribution of cadmium in soil and cacao beans in Peru</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Science of the Total Environment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/thomas2023-peru-cacao-cd-distribution">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup
